pos.personaBrief: Cruyff's Dream Team kept the ball moving ('moved and moved'), played out from the keeper and said dominating the ball means the opponent cannot score; possession was a means to progress, not an end in itself.

pro.personaBrief: Build-up always started from Zubizarreta and the pivot (Guardiola), even versus high presses, with close passing lines; occasional long switches by Koeman existed.

est.personaBrief: Cruyff's 3-4-3 relied on fixed positional occupation, with the opposite side holding positions, but with a false nine dropping, wingers moving inside and short close passing like rondos.

lar.personaBrief: Cruyff demanded maximum width: full-backs as traditional wide players and opposite-side players holding position, while wingers (Stoichkov) moved into central areas.

blo.personaBrief: Compact block and high line with the team pushed up, but sources say it rarely counter-pressed intensely; pressing 'like rats' by small players is noted.

mar.personaBrief: No direct marking evidence; the compact block, position exchanges and spatial structure point toward zonal organisation, and Cruyff showed little set-piece rigidity.

pla.personaBrief: Cruyff imposed his 3-4-3 model from 1988 on, played it against everyone, and before the 1994 final said Milan base the game on defence while we base ours on attack.

res.personaBrief: Cruyff preferred winning 5-4 to 1-0, told players to enjoy it in 1992, and attacked even in the 1994 final; spectacle and style over cautious results.

sis.personaBrief: Stars (Laudrup, Stoichkov, Romario) had defined roles in the system, which was built to turn technical players into a collective; Cruyff criticised stars who thought the team served them.

jog.personaBrief: Cruyff chose short technical players (Ferrer, Sergi, Amor), non-physical pivots like Guardiola, and technique over physicality; Laudrup as false nine/10.

bas.personaBrief: Cruyff gave Guardiola his debut in 1990/91 and used La Masia youngsters, but also signed stars like Koeman, Stoichkov, Romario, so title-winning mixed youth and signings.

lid.personaBrief: Cruyff was authoritative and tactically controlling, protected Stoichkov but clashed with stars and let Zubizarreta go; the 1994 dressing room imploded.
